extracted.intended_audience: cognitive neuroscience / psycholinguistics researchers studying humor (fMRI researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, selecting, and evaluating verbal-humor stimuli and their neural/behavioral responses in an event-related fMRI experiment that contrasts incongruity-resolution and absurd (partial-resolution) jokes. Includes stimulus controls, behavioral ratings, imaging preprocessing, and statistical-analysis standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-stage Model of Humor Processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor comprehension processing involves incongruity detection and resolution and then induces a feeling of amusement (detection → resolution → elaboration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The model specifies that (1) an individual detects the incongruity (supported by MTG and MFG activity), (2) reestablishes and reinterprets setup and punch line to resolve the incongruity (supported by SFG and IPL), and (3) perceives pleasure if the incongruity is comprehended (supported by vmPFC, bilateral amygdala, bilateral parahippocampal gyri). Primarily applies to incongruity-resolution humor; used as basis for experimental contrasts and behavioral ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual-Path Model: Incongruity-Resolution vs Absurd Humor
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed model that analyzes neural mechanisms underlying two humor kinds (incongruity-resolution humor and absurd humor) across the three stages, positing different subprocesses and neural circuits for each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies similarities (both detect incongruities) and differences: incongruity-resolution humor involves semantic processing, perspective taking, multi-sensory integration (TPJ, IPL, precuneus) leading to complete resolution and stronger elaboration (PCC, PHG); absurd humor involves phonological/semantic/word-level processing (fusiform, lingual gyrus, IFG), partial (pseudo) resolution and pragmatic/meta-comprehension (STG), with weaker elaboration. Use this framework to classify stimuli and interpret imaging/behavioral results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolvability of Incongruity (Classification Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify jokes by whether the incongruity can be fully resolved (incongruity-resolution humor) or only partially/pseudo-resolved (absurd humor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incongruity-resolution: 'playfully resolvable' by reinterpreting perspective or script; absurd: contains an absurdity opposed to reality/logic that cannot be completely resolved and leaves residual incongruity. Use examples (e.g., student standing on bill vs margarine becomes a butterfly) to determine class; resolvability drives expected neural and behavioral patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioral Rating Metrics: Surprise, Comprehensibility, Funniness
rubrics_metrics.description: Three types of ratings developed to reflect the three stages of humor processing: surprise (detection), comprehensibility (resolution), and funniness (elaboration/appreciation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used both in-scan and post-scan. In this study: in-scan funniness rating used a four-point Likert (1–4); post-scan ratings used 1–9 scales for surprise, comprehensibility, and funniness. Correlations between in-scan and post-scan ratings reported (e.g., r≈0.82–0.88). Use these metrics to quantify subjective responses and compare conditions (e.g., INC-RES > ABS > NEU on funniness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus Structure Requirement: Setup and Punch Line
rubrics_metrics.description: Each verbal stimulus must be divided into a setup and a punch line, where the setup forms a script/expectation and the punch line creates the incongruity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Setup provides cues to form expectations; punch line must deviate to create incongruity. For neutral controls, punch lines were rewritten to be unfunny but matched to humorous punch lines. Keep setup visible during punch-line presentation (as in paradigm) to allow rereading and integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linguistic Matching / Readability Control (CRIE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Control stimuli linguistic characteristics using the Chinese Readability Index Explorer (CRIE) across word, semantic, syntax, and cohesion levels to ensure differences in results reflect humor mechanisms rather than language features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRIE contains 31 indices; perform statistical tests (one-way ANOVA) across conditions to confirm no significant linguistic differences. This study reports no significant differences, enabling attribution of activation differences to humor processing rather than linguistic confounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus Selection and Quantitative Constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Select equal numbers of stimuli per condition and constrain length: e.g., 12 texts per stimulus type; setups ~39–42 words; punch lines ~10–11 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After strict filtering, choose balanced sets (here 12 per condition, total 48). Match mean word counts and variances across conditions to prevent length-driven effects. Document mean and SD for transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event-Related fMRI Paradigm Timing and Presentation Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an event-related within-subject design with randomized presentation and specific timing windows for setup, punch line, ratings, and jittered ISI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example timings used: Ready screen (8s), setup (14s), punch line (9s) with setup remaining visible, in-scan funniness rating (4s), jittered ISI 3.1–9.9s (M=6.2s). Four runs of ~6 min 8 s each; allow closed-eye breaks. Randomize stimuli order to avoid response habituation.

rubrics_metrics.name: fMRI Preprocessing and Quality-Control Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard preprocessing pipeline: slice timing, realignment, coregistration, normalization, smoothing; head motion exclusion criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply slice-timing correction (interleaved slices); realign to correct motion; co-register T1/T2 to EPI; normalize to MNI template; separate gray/white segments as needed; smooth with Gaussian kernel (example: 8 mm FWHM). Exclude subject data if head motion > ~3 mm (one voxel) on any translation or rotation parameter.

rubrics_metrics.name: fMRI Statistical Analysis and Non-Independence Controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Convolve event onsets with the canonical HRF and temporal derivative; perform whole-brain random-effects group analysis; avoid non-independence (double-dipping) in ROI analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use split-half analysis (odd runs to identify candidate regions, even runs to estimate BOLD change) to prevent circular analysis. Employ small volume correction (SVC) at extent threshold p<0.001 with specified ROI sphere (example: 8 mm radius). Report contrasts (INS-RES minus NEU, ABS minus NEU, INS-RES minus ABS, ABS minus INS-RES) and thresholding; example cluster-level correction: p<0.05 FWE with cluster size ≥10 voxels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrast Definitions for Hypothesis Testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Define specific contrasts to isolate detection, resolution, and elaboration processes: e.g., INS-RES vs NEU, ABS vs NEU, INS-RES vs ABS, ABS vs INS-RES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these contrasts to map condition-specific activations and to interpret which neural regions correspond to detection, resolution, or elaboration. Report voxel coordinates, BA, z-scores, and cluster sizes for transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neural-Process Mapping Guidance (Interpretation Criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Map particular psychological subprocesses to brain regions to interpret results: e.g., TPJ/IPL → integration/coherence building; precuneus → perspective taking; PCC → episodic memory retrieval; PHG → feeling of amusement; IFG/fusiform/lingual/STG → phonological/semantic/word processing and pragmatic awareness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these mappings as interpretive criteria when evaluating whether a joke elicited semantic/perspective-based resolution (incongruity-resolution) vs word-level/phonological processing and pragmatic meta-comprehension (absurd). Cross-validate with behavioral ratings (surprise, comprehensibility, funniness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioral Statistical Analysis Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze behavioral ratings with appropriate repeated-measures statistics and post hoc tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: one-way repeated-measures ANOVA for differences among INC-RES, ABS, and NEU on surprise, comprehensibility, funniness; use Bonferroni post hoc tests for pairwise comparisons; report F, p, and effect sizes (η^2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Example-based Operationalization of Resolution Processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Operationalize how participants resolve incongruities via processes like rereading, perspective switching, semantic reanalysis, or phonological/semantic word processing depending on humor type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use worked examples (e.g., 'Teacher: Why are you late?... No. I was standing on it.' for complete resolution via perspective change and elaboration; 'margarine thrown out of a window becomes a butterfly' for partial resolution via semantic/phonological mapping) to guide stimulus coding, pilot testing, and annotation of stimuli for expected process type.
